# Draft:2025 global trade war

A global trade war began on April 9, 2025, after the United States imposed reciprocal tariffs on every country.
Background
Second Trump tariffs
In March 2025, president Donald Trump imposed an additional ten percent tariff on imports from China and a 25% tariff on most imports from Canada and Mexico, raising fears of a global trade war.
Course of the trade war
Steel and aluminum tariffs (March 2025)
On March 12, 2025, a 25% tariff on all imported steel and aluminum in the United States came into effect. The following day, Trump threatened to impose a 200% tariff on alcoholic beverages imported from the European Union after it retaliated against the steel and aluminum tariffs; by the threats, a global trade war had begun, according to The Wall Street Journal. After Trump announced a 25% tariff on imported automobiles, The Washington Post described it as a potentially "major escalation in Trump's global trade war".
Reciprocal tariffs (April 2025)
On April 9, 2025, Trump's reciprocal tariffs took effect, intensifying the global trade war.
